title: Founder Clarity — Stripe-Era Quarterly Brief
description: A left-anchored quarterly-update layout built on strict grid discipline, Inter-weight hierarchy, and a single oversized KPI card — channeling Stripe's investor-deck restraint rather than flashy infographic energy.
philosophy: This template treats whitespace as a trust signal: the wider the margin, the more confident the speaker. It refuses centered headlines, decorative accents, and multi-chart chaos in favor of one clear truth per slide delivered with typographic authority. It is designed for founders standing in front of boards and operators briefing executive leadership — people who read the deck before the meeting and arrive ready to act. Every element earns its position by carrying informational load; nothing decorates.
goodFor: Quarterly investor and board update decks
Single-KPI spotlight slides within a larger executive deck
avoidFor: Consumer-facing sales or marketing pitch decks
High-image editorial or brand storytelling sections
Casual all-hands with an informal, emoji-forward tone
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide channels boardroom austerity — Stripe-era restraint where abundant negative space signals speaker confidence rather than incomplete design. Asymmetric left-anchored composition lets a dense typographic block face an open, unhurried right field, creating quiet visual tension without any decorative device. The overall feeling is serious, precise, and unhurried: a founder who arrives prepared and needs no flourish to command attention. Avoid centered layouts, gradient fills, icon clusters, illustrative motifs, or any diagonal element — drama lives exclusively in weight contrast and the discipline of the grid.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; title block and subtitle anchor to cols 1–7, leaving the right ~40% as deliberate void — the emptiness is load-bearing, not an accident. Outer margin holds at roughly 10% on all four sides, with the left edge serving as the primary alignment rail for every text element. A small quarter/period label or deck-category caption sits above the title separated by a single hairline rule, establishing the informational hierarchy before the eye reaches the headline. No page number on the title slide; the sole bottom element is a presenter or company attribution flushed hard-left.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a board memo printed on heavy stock — unhurried, load-bearing, and quietly confident. One oversized metric dominates the left-center mass, given so much spatial authority that the surrounding silence reads as editorial intent, not emptiness. Supporting context lines sit to its right in a tighter column, subordinate in scale but aligned to the same invisible baseline grid, creating asymmetric tension rather than symmetry. Avoid any decorative rule flourishes, gradient fills, icon clusters, or centered compositions; the discipline is the aesthetic.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a fixed left rail occupying cols 1–2 as dead margin (≈8% of canvas width), leaving all live content in cols 3–12. Slide divides horizontally into two unequal bands: an oversized KPI card anchored left in the upper two-thirds (spanning cols 3–7), with a supporting label stack or 2–3 terse callout lines occupying cols 8–11 at mid-height. A single 1px rule separates the KPI zone from a bottom-strip footnote or period label. Slide number sits bottom-right in the dead-margin equivalent on the right edge; no header band.
